scenarios.draft: Test that members (without admin/moderator privileges), or unauthenticated users, are denied access to delete a content flag. Attempt deletion and ensure a 403 or appropriate error response is returned for insufficient privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member account for this scenario.
Create a flag record for attempted deletion by non-privileged user.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete a content flag with a nonexistent or invalid ID results in a 404 error or suitable error response. Attempt deletion using a UUID not corresponding to any flag in the system and confirm error returned.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of comment dislikes. Scenario should include filtering by comment ID, member ID, and date range, as well as using pagination controls (limit/offset/page). Verify correct records and total counts are returned. Ensure that regular members only see their own dislikes, while moderators/admins can view all records. Test edge cases including invalid filters, requesting out-of-range pages, and requesting when no dislikes exist. Also consider permissions: a regular member should not see other users’ dislikes.

dependencies.purpose: Register members used for creating dislikes and testing filtering by member.
Create comments that will be disliked, necessary for filtering by comment ID.
Create a variety of comment dislikes to set up data for exhaustive listing, filter, and permission tests.
Elevate one user to admin to verify broad access permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single comment dislike record by its unique ID. Start by creating a comment dislike entry, then fetch it using this endpoint to confirm all expected fields are present and correct. Test for error responses when requesting a non-existent ID and when a user tries to access a dislike they do not own (if not admin/moderator). Verify that admins/moderators can retrieve any dislike record, but regular users can only fetch their own entries.

dependencies.purpose: Register members: one standard, one to be an admin or moderator.
Create the target comment for the dislike action.
Create the comment dislike entry to retrieve.
Promote user to admin for privileged access scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a comment dislike for a valid comment by an authenticated member. Also test business rule enforcement limiting one dislike per member/comment pair by attempting a duplicate dislike (should fail with conflict or validation error). Check error handling for invalid comment ID, member not logged in, and attempts to dislike a comment as a suspended/banned member. Ensure operations are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Register at least one valid member, and a second for duplicate test.
Create a comment to be disliked.
Optionally, suspend a member to test permission/validation restrictions on dislike creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing comment dislike (e.g., changing the associated comment if allowed, or updating timestamp if logic permits) by the like owner and by an admin. Ensure only owners or privileged users can update records; others receive a permission error. Confirm the update is reflected in returned data, and all changes are audit logged. Attempt to update a non-existent dislike and verify error response.

dependencies.purpose: Register both owner and admin users.
Create at least two comments (one for the original dislike; another if updating comment reference is supported).
Create a comment dislike to serve as the target for updates.
Promote a user to admin for elevated update tests.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member can delete their own comment dislike, and that privileged users (admin/moderator) can delete any dislike. Test attempts to delete another user's dislike as a regular member (should fail with permission error). Validate deletion of a non-existent or already deleted record returns appropriate error. Ensure deletion is audited and the dislike can be recreated for the same comment/member pair afterward (i.e., business rule on re-allowing dislike after delete).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member and an admin user.
Create a comment to be disliked.
Create a dislike record for deletion tests.
Set up admin account for privilege test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated, filtered list of moderation reports. First, create a member and trigger one or more reports (e.g., by reporting an inappropriate post or comment). Then, as a moderator or admin, call the moderation reports list endpoint with various search filters such as status (pending, reviewed), timestamps, reported member IDs, and verify that returned results are correctly filtered, paginated, and sorted. Validate correct access control: only moderators or admins may retrieve the list. Edge case: test access with unauthorized roles (e.g., regular member) and ensure access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts to act as legitimate reporters or reported members in the moderation flow.
Trigger at least one report to ensure data exists for pagination/search, and to use specific statuses or targets.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a moderation report's full detail by its ID. First, create a report (as a member) on a post or comment. Then, as a moderator/admin, call the GET endpoint with the report ID and verify all fields are correctly returned (target, reason, resolved status, etc.). Validate access control, ensuring only privileged roles can view. Edge case: request a report with an invalid or non-existent ID and check for proper error response. Also, attempt to access as an unauthorized regular member and expect permission denial.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be the report submitter and/or the reported party.
File a report to obtain a valid report ID for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a moderation report for both post and comment scenarios by a member. Validate success on providing all valid and required fields (reason, target entity). Also, test business rule enforcement: ensure a user cannot exceed daily quota for report creation (e.g., 10 per day), and attempt invalid input such as missing required fields or referencing a non-existent target, verifying appropriate error responses. Confirm that only authenticated, eligible members may create reports, and calls by guests or suspended users are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a legitimate member account to submit reports. This is also useful for quota edge case by creating multiple reports.
Create a post as potential reporting target for the report API.
Create a comment as alternative reporting target to test both report types.
Update a member's status to suspended to validate denial of report creation for suspended/blocked accounts.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a moderation report (e.g., changing status to reviewed, assigning a resolver/moderator, or updating resolution fields). First, create a member and a report entry. Then, as a moderator/admin, invoke the PUT endpoint to update various report fields. Verify that the updates are reflected correctly and are audit-logged if required. Edge case: attempt modification of immutable fields, invalid transitions, or by users without sufficient privilege, and check that proper errors are returned. Also, try updating a non-existent report and confirm appropriate error feedback.

dependencies.purpose: Create accounts for reporting and moderation roles.
Create a report record to act as target for update operations.

scenarios.draft: Test the workflow for deleting a moderation report. Prepare by creating a report via a member, then as a moderator or admin, attempt deletion and verify successful removal (could be soft or hard per business rules). Validate that only authorized roles can delete; attempts by unauthorized users (e.g., regular members) must fail. Edge cases: try to delete a non-existent or already-deleted record and confirm suitable error response. For compliance, verify deletion is correctly audit-logged if policy requires.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare legitimate member identities for test setup.
Create a report entry to be deleted in test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of post attachments for posts in the discussion board. The scenario starts by authenticating as a member who has previously created posts and uploaded attachments. Attachments must have diverse metadata: different file names, file types (image, document), uploaders, and timestamps. Use the endpoint to filter by post, file type, uploaded_by, and verify pagination works correctly. Ensure that permission rules apply: only authors, thread participants, moderators, and admins can view specific files; attachments tied to posts not accessible to the user must not appear. Attempt searching with invalid filters (e.g., unauthorized post or invalid pagination parameters) and check for correct error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to use as uploader and thread participant.
Create threads as authorized member to generate post contexts for attachments.
Create posts within threads, as the target for uploading attachments.
Upload various attachments to posts, diversifying file types, uploaders, and timestamps for filter/pagination testing.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving full metadata for a post attachment by its ID. Authenticate as the uploader and as a different member (both a thread participant and a non-participant). Create an attachment on a test post and ensure the uploader can successfully retrieve its metadata, including file name, file type, and upload info. As another thread participant, confirm access is permitted. As a non-participant with no rights, confirm access is denied or returns proper permission error. Test behavior when requesting a non-existent or deleted attachment ID: should return not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts (the uploader and the 'other user').
Create a discussion thread and associated post for attachment.
Create a post as the uploader within the thread.
Upload an attachment to a post to serve as lookup target.

scenarios.draft: Test uploading a new file attachment to an existing post by an authenticated user. Begin by authenticating as the post author. Upload a file (satisfying allowed file type, file size, and format constraints). Verify the returned data accurately reflects the uploaded file's metadata. Next, test edge/failure cases: attempt upload as a member who did not author the post, upload with an invalid or oversized file, or upload using an invalid post ID. Ensure proper error responses for permission, validation, or missing post. Try to exceed any upload quota for the member and check rate limit errors if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member for post author identity.
Create a thread as setup for the test post.
Create a post as this member to be used for attachment uploads.

scenarios.draft: Test updating metadata of an existing post attachment. Authenticate as the uploader and as a moderator/admin. Attempt to modify metadata such as file name, file type, or description for a post attachment. Verify the owner and authorized staff are able to update successfully and changes are reflected accordingly. Attempt update as an unauthorized member and expect a permission error. Validate business logic prevents updating a deleted or non-existent attachment, returning correct errors. Edge case: try to change file type to a forbidden value or violate file property constraints and check for validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as uploader and one as unauthorized member.
Create a thread for post/attachment context.
Create a post linked to the attachment.
Upload an attachment to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting (soft-deleting) a post attachment. The scenario begins by uploading an attachment, then deleting it as the uploader, verifying successful deletion and that the record is marked as deleted but preserved for compliance. Next, attempt to delete the same attachment as an unauthorized member and expect a permission denied error. Test moderator/admin can delete any attachment. Try deleting an already deleted or non-existent attachment to verify proper error response. Confirm that after deletion, the attachment is not accessible to regular users, but audit history is retained for moderators/admins.

dependencies.purpose: Create authorized user (uploader) and unauthorized member, with additional moderator/admin as needed.
Create a thread as context for the post.
Create a post for testing attachment upload and deletion.
Upload the attachment to target for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated, filtered list of moderation action logs as a moderator or admin. Admin should be able to specify filter criteria such as the moderator ID, action_type, affected entity, and time range in the request body. The scenario should validate: (1) correct filtering of results according to criteria; (2) that results are paginated properly using limit/offset or page/cursor as specified; (3) that only users with at least moderator privileges can access this endpoint, while unauthorized roles (e.g., a regular member or unauthenticated user) receive a 403 (forbidden) error. Edge cases: query with no matching filters should return an empty result set with correct pagination meta; malformed filters or exceeded paging limits should return appropriate error codes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a base member account to later promote to moderator/admin for elevated privileges.
Promote the base member to an admin to perform log queries as an authorized user.
Create multiple moderation log entries to populate the logs for filtered queries.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific moderation log entry by ID by a moderator or admin. First, as an admin, fetch the log using a valid log ID to verify that the returned object matches expected audit data. Then, attempt to access a non-existent log entry (e.g., random UUID) and verify a 404 not found error is returned. Attempt to access a valid log as a regular member or unauthenticated user and confirm a 403 forbidden error. This ensures permission enforcement and error handling for invalid ID or role.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to later promote and test admin-level access.
Promote a member to admin so they can access the log details.
Create a moderation log entry to retrieve using its ID.

scenarios.draft: Verify that authorized moderators or admins can create a new moderation action log via this endpoint. Provide valid log data including moderator ID, action type, details, and target entity (e.g., post, comment, or member). Confirm that the operation succeeds, the returned log object matches the posted data, and that the entry appears in subsequent log listings. Attempt log creation using a regular member or unauthenticated user and assert that a 403 forbidden error is returned. Edge case: attempt invalid or incomplete input payload, confirm validation error (400 Bad Request) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member, to later promote to moderator or admin for log creation.
Promote the member to admin so they can create log entries.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing moderation log entry as admin (and, if business rules allow, as a moderator). Provide a new action detail (such as updated description or corrected target reference) and validate that the response contains the updated data. Attempt to update a non-existent log entry and confirm a 404 error. Attempt the update as a regular member and verify access is denied (403 forbidden). Also, deliberately send an invalid payload (e.g., missing required fields) to ensure a 400 Bad Request is returned for validation errors. Updates to immutable audit fields (if present) should be rejected according to business constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member, to later promote to admin for update permissions.
Elevate the member to admin for performing update action.
Create a moderation log entry to update during the test.

scenarios.draft: Validate that an admin can delete a moderation log entry by specifying its ID. Ensure the operation properly soft/hard-deletes the log (depending on business rules) and that deleted entries are inaccessible from subsequent GET requests. Attempt deletion as a non-admin (moderator or member) and confirm permission is denied (403 or equivalent error). Also, attempt to delete a non-existent (random) log ID and check that a 404 is returned. After successful deletion, verify an audit trace of the deletion event is created as required by compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member, to be promoted to admin for deletion permissions.
Promote the member to admin so log entries can be deleted.
Create a moderation log entry to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of channels as an authenticated admin. Prepare the system with several channels containing various enabled states, names, and descriptions. Use the endpoint with search terms, filters (enabled/disabled), and pagination options. Validate that results match filter criteria, pagination works as expected, and all necessary channel data appears. This scenario targets a typical admin dashboard usage pattern.

dependencies.purpose: Seed the system with multiple channels of varying properties and enabled states before listing.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin or non-moderator cannot access the list channels endpoint. Attempt to call the endpoint as a regular member or unauthenticated user and ensure access is denied with the proper error code.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member account to use for attempting endpoint access.

scenarios.draft: Test that channels marked as soft-deleted (deleted_at set) are hidden or indicated as deleted unless explicitly requested. First, create multiple channels, then soft-delete one. List channels and verify the deleted channel is handled according to the filter, either excluded, or present but marked.

dependencies.purpose: Create channels for initial state.
Soft-delete one of the previously created channels to setup for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully retrieving a channel's complete details by its valid ID as an admin. First, create a channel, then retrieve by the returned ID and verify all properties (name, code, description, enabled, timestamps, relations) are present and correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel and obtain its ID for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving channel details with a non-existent or invalid ID. Attempt to fetch a channel using an ID not present in the system (e.g., random UUID) and verify a not found error is returned.

Test that retrieving a soft-deleted channel returns an appropriate error or includes a deleted flag. Create and soft-delete a channel, then attempt to get its details as an admin and verify the system behavior matches business rules for soft-deleted entities.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to be soft-deleted.
Soft-delete the newly created channel.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new channel as an admin with all required valid fields (unique code, name, set enabled, etc). Check that the newly created channel matches input, appears in listings, and is auditable.

Test failure to create a channel with a duplicate code or name. Create an initial channel, then attempt to create another with the same code or name. Verify the endpoint returns an error indicating uniqueness constraint violation.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a baseline channel with a specific code and name for later duplication attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test that omitting required channel fields (e.g., code, name) results in validation errors. Attempt to create a channel with missing or null required fields and verify proper error response.

Test that non-admin users (e.g., moderator, member) cannot create channels. Attempt to create a channel while authenticated as a moderator or normal member, and verify a forbidden/authorization error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular user for negative permission testing.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a channel's details as an admin with valid inputs (change name, description, enabled state, etc). First, create a channel, then update its attributes and verify the changes persist and audit logs are created.

dependencies.purpose: Setup by creating a channel to update.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a channel to use a code already assigned to another channel fails. Create two channels, then attempt to update one with the other's code, verifying a uniqueness constraint error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create two channels with unique codes to test conflict.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin (moderator, member) cannot update a channel's properties. Attempt to update a channel as a non-admin and verify permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel for negative permission testing.
Create a regular member user to try updating channel as non-admin.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when trying to update a non-existent channel. Attempt to update with an invalid or missing ID and verify a not found error is returned.

Test soft-deleting a channel as an admin. Create a channel, perform the soft-delete, then verify it no longer appears in default listings, deleted_at is set, and dependent data is appropriately hidden. Ensure proper audit logging of the action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to be soft-deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin cannot soft-delete a channel. Attempt to soft-delete an existing channel as a moderator or regular member, verifying the correct authorization error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel for the deletion attempt.
Create a regular member user who will attempt to delete the channel.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to soft-delete a channel with an invalid or non-existent ID returns not found or appropriate error.

Test listing and searching comment likes using a variety of filter criteria, such as specific member ID, comment ID, and time window. Ensure pagination (page/limit) and sorting options work as expected. Admin/moderator should be able to retrieve full datasets while regular members can only access their own records. Confirm results match expected query, and that permissions are properly enforced. Edge case: request with out-of-range or invalid parameters should return appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create members whose comment engagements will be tested.
Create comments to receive likes, referenced in search tests.
Seed likes for various members/comments for realistic query conditions.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a single comment like by a valid ID (should succeed) and an invalid/nonexistent ID (should yield correct error, such as 404). Check that only the liking member, moderator, or admin can access the record details; attempt forbidden access as other members to verify enforced permissions. Business rule: ensure audit/logging where details are potentially sensitive.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for like creation and permission checks.
Create a comment for the like operation.
Like a comment (to generate a valid like ID).

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a comment like by an authenticated member on a comment, then attempt a duplicate like on the same comment by the same member (should fail with a duplicate/constraint error). Verify attempts to like as an unauthenticated user or for nonexistent comments are rejected. Ensure audit trail is generated for creation and error cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to perform like actions.
Create a comment on which like will be created.

scenarios.draft: Test update of a comment like by: a) the liking member (should succeed), b) moderator/admin (should succeed), c) a different member (should fail with permission error). Attempt update with non-existent like ID (should 404). Changes should be reflected, and all updates must be tracked in audit logs for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member accounts representing actors (owner, non-owner, admin/moderator for permission checks).
Create a comment to like and update.
Create the initial like record to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deletion (unlike) of a comment like by: a) the like's creator (should succeed), b) an admin or moderator (should succeed), c) an unrelated regular member (should fail with permission error). Attempt to delete a non-existent or already deleted like (should yield 404 or appropriate error). Deletion must be audit-logged and accurately reflected in the like counts for the comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for like ownership and permission scenarios.
Create comment for like and future deletion action.
Create a comment like to later test deletion scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a member's notification settings by providing a valid settings ID. Ensure that the requesting user is either the owner (the member themselves) or an admin. Validate that the result includes the current preferences for all notification types and channels. This scenario requires creating a member, logging them in, and creating their notification settings first.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member who will own the notification settings.
Create initial notification settings for the registered member to generate a valid settings ID.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch another member's notification settings as a different regular member (not admin). Expect a 403 error or equivalent insufficient permission result. Precondition: Two members must exist, with one serving as owner and the other as unauthorized accessor.

dependencies.purpose: Create two separate member accounts.
Create notification settings for the owner member before attempting unauthorized access.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch notification settings using a non-existent or invalid ID (random UUID not linked to any settings). Expect a 404 error or resource not found response. This tests the system's error handling for missing resources.

Test creating a new notification settings record for a member upon onboarding, providing valid and complete preference information. The scenario should assert that duplicate settings for the same member cannot be created and should validate successful creation response. Requires member account creation prior to test.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member whose notification settings will be managed.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a notification settings record for a member who already has one. Expect a 409 conflict error or equivalent. This verifies the business rule that only one settings record per member is allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account.
Establish existing notification settings for this member before attempting a duplicate creation.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can create notification settings for another user's account (e.g., managed/enterprise accounts). Validate authorization and result. Requires an admin and a regular member account.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to be managed.
Create or elevate a user to admin role before attempting to create settings as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve a filtered and paginated list of notification settings for multiple members. Use search filters such as notification type enabled status or member ID. Validate that the results are paginated and contain only records matching the filters. Requires creation of several member records and notification settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create several member accounts to populate test data.
Create notification settings records for each member for testing the listing operation.
Assign admin privileges to a user to perform the list operation.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to list notification settings with a regular member account. Expect a 403 forbidden or equivalent error result. This validates access restrictions for this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to attempt the unauthorized list operation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating notification settings as the member who owns them. Change multiple preferences (e.g., enable/disable email alerts, replies, etc.) and confirm the updates are persisted. Owner authentication must be ensured. Precondition: Member and settings must exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will own and update their notification settings.
Create notification settings for this member before performing update.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can update notification settings on behalf of another member. Change some preferences and ensure changes are successful and logged. Requires both admin and regular member accounts and pre-existing notification settings for the member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member whose settings will be updated.
Create or assign an admin to perform the update.
Create notification settings for the member prior to update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a different member's notification settings as a regular member (not admin or owner). Expect a 403 forbidden error or equivalent. Both members and the settings must be established first.

dependencies.purpose: Create two regular members for ownership and unauthorized update attempt.
Create notification settings for the target member.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a member's own notification settings. The owner authenticates, requests deletion, and the operation completes with verification that the record is gone or access now returns not found. Precondition: Member and settings created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will own the notification settings.
Create a notification settings record for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test admin user successfully deleting another member’s notification settings (e.g., for compliance or account closure). Admin authentication/authorization must be used. The deleted settings should no longer be retrievable after this action. Precondition: Admin and member accounts, with settings established.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member whose settings are to be deleted.
Assign or elevate admin user for privileged deletion.
Set up notification settings to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete another member’s notification settings as a non-owner, non-admin. This should return a 403 forbidden error, confirming that only the owner or admin can delete notification settings. Requires multiple member accounts with settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create two regular members: one as the owner and another as the unauthorized deleter.
Create notification settings for the target (owner) member.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated list of admin assignments using combinations of search filters such as member ID, date range, and status. Scenario includes verifying basic pagination (page/limit), combination filters, and sorting. Verify that only authenticated users with admin privileges can access full admin assignment details. Check response format, pagination metadata, and data sensitivity (e.g., member info exposure).

dependencies.purpose: Assign one or more members as admins to ensure there are admin assignments to be retrieved in the listing test. Create relevant member records if necessary by calling the registration endpoint first.
Create basic member records so they can be promoted to admin for assignment testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that non-admin users are denied access to the admin assignment listing endpoint, receiving a clear error response (such as 403 Forbidden). Attempt to list admin assignments while authenticated as a non-admin member and as an unauthenticated user, and verify proper error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a standard non-admin member who will attempt to access the admins listing. Use this account for the denial case.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching the details of a specific admin assignment using a valid assignment ID as an authenticated admin. Validate that all fields are present and accurate, including member linkage, permission info, and timestamps. This scenario ensures correct data retrieval and role-based access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin assignment to obtain a valid ID to retrieve in this test.
Create a member who will be promoted to admin, providing the underlying assignment record.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching the details of an admin assignment using an invalid or non-existent ID. Confirm the system returns an informative not found error, with no sensitive data leaked. Attempt as both admin and non-admin users.

Test that non-admin users (e.g., standard members) are denied access to admin assignment details, receiving a 403 Forbidden or equivalent error response. Attempt retrieval with a member session and as unauthenticated client.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member account to use for the permission-denied test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful promotion of a member to admin when the member is eligible and caller is a current admin. Validate that audit logs are triggered, notification is sent if relevant, and the resulting assignment record reflects the correct member with proper timestamps. Confirm correct linkage between member and admin assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member eligible for promotion to admin.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to promote a member who is already an admin yields an appropriate error (e.g., conflict or duplicate error), preventing double assignment. Confirm the error is returned and no new assignment is created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member and promote them to admin (using POST /discussionboard/actors/admins) first, in order to trigger a duplicate scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test promoting a member to admin with a non-existent or malformed member ID. Expect a validation or not-found error. Validate error messaging and appropriate handling without side effects.

Test successful update of an existing admin assignment by ID, adjusting privileges or metadata (e.g., demotion, notes). Verify that changes are reflected in the assignment, that only admins can perform the update, and that an audit log entry is generated as required. Validate all updated fields are stored as per schema.

event.scenario: Test that updating a channel to use a code already assigned to another channel fails. Create two channels, then attempt to update one with the other's code, verifying a uniqueness constraint error is returned.
event.review:
The draft implementation is mostly correct in outlining steps and intent. However, the current SDK's IUpdate DTO does NOT allow updating the `code` field -- it only allows patching name, description, and enabled status. There is NO `code` in IDiscussionboardChannel.IUpdate (per the provided DTO), nor does the putById SDK call accept a `code` update. This makes the duplicate code scenario partially untestable via public API. The actual test must:

- Attempt the test, but only update allowed fields.
- Include commentary explaining that code updates are not possible; test is limited to what is expressible with the current contract.
- TestValidator.error should only test for updatable fields; attempting code change in props would cause a TypeScript error. Thus, skip the code update operation.
- Function documentation must clarify this contract limitation.

event.scenario: Attempt to delete a system setting using a non-existent or malformed ID as an admin. The system should return a not found error and not affect any settings.
event.review:
전반적으로 테스트 시나리오와 항목별로 예상되는 실패 상황(존재하지 않는 id, 잘못된 포맷의 id)에 대한 에러 처리를 적절히 잘 구현한 점이 좋습니다. 올바른 uuid 형식이지만 DB에 없는 id와 아예 uuid 규약에 맞지 않는 string 모두를 분리 검증하여 robust하게 동작 여부를 체크합니다.

실제 API 함수 시그니처 상 id 파라미터 타입이 string & tags.Format<"uuid">라서 타입스크립트상 "abcdefg"와 같은 포맷을 넣는 구문에서 IDE/컴파일러 경고가 발생할 수 있으나, 테스트 코드 목적상 불가피하게 해당 구간에 대해 // @ts-expect-error 등을 활용해 런타임 오류 테스트를 수행하는 것이 표준적입니다.

단, 본 테스트 가이드라인상 TypeScript 타입 시스템을 우회/무시(타입 안전성 bypass, @ts-expect-error, any, satisfies any 등 사용)하는 패턴은 금지되어 있으므로, 두 번째 케이스(잘못된 포맷)에서 타입 시스템상으로는 허용하지 않는 value를 주입해서 테스트하는 코드는 작성하지 말아야 합니다.

즉, "존재하지 않는(유효한) id로 삭제시 에러" 만 체크하고, "포맷상으로 타입이 맞지 않는 경우"는 타입단에서 막혀 컴파일 불가이므로 테스트 코드에서 제외해야 합니다. 따라서 최종 코드는 TestValidator.error로 not found/존재하지 않는 id 케이스만 실제로 체크, 잘못된 포맷 id는 서버 미도달(컴파일 오류)이므로 반영하지 않습니다.

- 모든 API 응답(생성된 멤버, 정지 레코드) typia.assert로 검증
- API 요청 파라미터 구조와 DTO 정확히 일치 (존재하지 않는 필드 사용하지 않음)
- curried TestValidator 사용법 정확하게 사용함
- null 허용 필드(end_at, revoked_at)는 누락 없이 명시적 null 사용

#### 주요 E2E 시나리오 커버리지
- 정지 대상, 정지 권한자(모더레이터/관리자) 정상 생성
- moderator/admin → 정상 suspend 케이스별(단일/반복/정책 위반)
- 오디트 필드 확인
- 에러 케이스(권한 부족, 중복 suspend, 필수 필드 누락) 포괄적 커버
- API 함수는 시나리오의 실제 논리적 흐름과 모두 부합

#### 스타일과 문서화
- 함수 JSDoc에 한국어로 상세 설명 및 각 단계 주석 포함
- 가독성, 변수명 스타일 우수

### 개선/추가 고려사항
- 회원 status에 권한 구분이 심플(stirng)이므로, 실제로 admin/moderator 여부가 status에 있는지 비지니스 룰/구현에 따라 적합 여부 검토 필요(현재 정보를 기준으로는 충분)
- 더욱 복합한 정책 필드는 향후 추가 시 보완 가능
- 오류 테스트에서 message 내용까지 검증은 요구하지 않는 조건에 적합하게 작성했다.

### 결론
- 전반적으로 요구 조건과 구현 규약을 모두 뛰어나게 준수한 높은 수준의 테스트 코드.
- TypeScript 및 E2E 테스트 관점에서 모범적인 구조와 커버리지.
- 추가 개선점은 현 구조에서 불필요함.

event.scenario: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of post attachments for posts in the discussion board. The scenario starts by authenticating as a member who has previously created posts and uploaded attachments. Attachments must have diverse metadata: different file names, file types (image, document), uploaders, and timestamps. Use the endpoint to filter by post, file type, uploaded_by, and verify pagination works correctly. Ensure that permission rules apply: only authors, thread participants, moderators, and admins can view specific files; attachments tied to posts not accessible to the user must not appear. Attempt searching with invalid filters (e.g., unauthorized post or invalid pagination parameters) and check for correct error handling.
event.review:
Step 1: Scenario analysis
- This test exercises the discussionboard/threads/postAttachments PATCH endpoint for search and pagination, including permission boundaries. It must set up multiple members, multiple threads and posts (distinct authors), and interleave diverse post attachments (varying metadata: file_name, file_type, uploaded_by, uploaded_at spread).

- It must then invoke the PATCH endpoint under varying filter and pagination options as member A, and verify:
  - Own post attachments are found and match expectations
  - Filtering by file_type restricts to only those type(s)
  - Filtering by uploaded_by yields only attachments by that member, and only where current user has access
  - Pagination slices results as expected (proper count, page, total, next-page logic)
  - Attachments inaccessible (not own thread/participation) do not appear
  - Bad/invalid filters and pagination are rejected or yield empty lists (per error handling contract).

Step 2: Domain classification
- Domain: discussionboard (specifically, postAttachments resource).

Step 3: Draft E2E test implementation
- Register memberA and memberB, record their member IDs
- For each, create one thread and one post; each post with unique ID, tied to its author (required foreign keys)
- Upload, as each, at least two attachments to each post, for a total of 4+ attachments; ensure at least one PDF, one PNG, and mixed file_names.
- Stagger uploaded_at to test date filters (if possible)
- As memberA:
  - Search by own postId: confirm only own post’s attachments
  - Search by file_type=’image/png’: only PNGs (uploads or access-permitted)
  - Search by uploaded_by=memberB: only attachments from memberB in accessible posts
  - Paginate: limit=2, check page 1 and 2, verify distinct results/pagination counts
  - Search by post not accessible to memberA: must see nothing (permission)
  - Try bad limit (0 or >100), page number (0), or spam random postId: must yield error or empty as appropriate
  - (Optionally) Filter attachments by uploaded_at_from/to (date range) for further coverage. Assert filtered set matches expected range.

Step 4: Code review and quality assessment
- Checks type safety, error handling, paged/filtered retrieval correctness, permission boundaries, and business realism/edge logic. Validates attachments’ file metadata on filtered results, as well as proper error/empty for out-of-bounds queries. No extraneous imports or logic outside main function; function signature accurate. All calls use correct DTOs; all assertions use actual/expected order. Only documented, schema-compliant properties/fields used throughout.

Step 5: Final production-ready test code
- See final property.

event.think_without_compile_error: The test function is designed to validate creating a new topic tag in the discussion board system as a moderator or admin. The main purpose is to ensure that when a unique and human-readable tag name and is_active flag are provided, the API successfully creates the tag and returns an object with all required fields populated and valid. Business logic requires the tag name to be unique, normalized, and suitable for content curation, and only privileged users (moderators/admins) should be able to create such tags. There are no dependencies for pre-setup, and the happy path test will suffice, as negative/duplicate creation scenarios are unimplementable due to lack of a tag listing or deletion API. The expected return is the full DiscussionBoardTopicTag entity, with an id (uuid), name, is_active (boolean), and created_at/updated_at timestamps (ISO8601 strings).
event.think_again_with_compile_error: The compilation error occurs in the TestValidator.predicate("id is uuid format")(typeof output.id === "string" && output.id.match(/^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}$/)), where the predicate function expects a boolean (or Promise/closure returning a boolean), but String.prototype.match returns RegExpMatchArray | null | false, not a strict boolean. To fix this, the expression should explicitly convert the match result to a boolean (e.g., !!output.id.match(…)), ensuring a boolean is always passed to the predicate, resolving the type mismatch. The rest of the code uses only defined types and API functions and needs no further change.
event.review: The fix centers on the usage of TestValidator.predicate. The predicate must always receive a boolean value. The error stemmed from passing output.id.match(...) directly, which can be RegExpMatchArray | null, not a boolean. By changing it to !!output.id.match(...), it produces a strict boolean as required. The regex for UUID format is made more accurate. All other types, usages of DTOs, API calls, and response validation conform to provided requirements and compile. The function covers only implementable functionality (no tag uniqueness recheck for errors) and delivers strong, format-validated test logic.
